faq.title: Answers to the questions we get most

items.title: Do you charge seafarers a fee?
items.text: No. Placement is paid by the principal. Under MLC 2006, no manning agency may charge a seafarer for recruitment or placement.

items.title: How long does registration take?
items.text: The form takes about five minutes. Document verification is usually completed within two working days.

items.title: Which ranks do you place?
items.text: Deck, engine, and hotel ranks from ratings to master and chief engineer, across container, tanker, gas, bulk, offshore, and cruise tonnage.

items.title: How fast can a crew request be answered?
items.text: A first shortlist is typically returned within one working day of receiving a complete specification.

insights.title: Navigating career opportunities in global shipping
insights.lede: International shipping underpins world trade. Learn how deck and engine officers can move into tanker and LNG fleets for long-term growth.
insights.body:
Where the demand sits today

The global fleet keeps growing faster than the pipeline of qualified officers, and that gap is most obvious in tanker, gas carrier, and offshore tonnage. Shipping companies that once hired almost exclusively from Europe and the Philippines now source heavily from Indonesia, India, and Eastern Europe. For an Indonesian officer with a clean record and current certificates, that means more choice of vessels, flags, and salary packages than at any point in the last decade.

Container shipping remains the largest single employer of deck and engine officers, but it is also the most cyclical. Tanker and LNG contracts tend to be longer and less exposed to the same demand swings, which is one reason we see officers use a container contract as a first step and then move into tankers once they have a couple of years of sea time behind them.

Building a credible seafaring CV

Ship managers read a CV for two things: can this person actually do the rank, and will they pass the principal's screening. Both come down to how clearly the sea service is laid out. Every contract should show the vessel type, gross tonnage, engine or kW, rank held, dates, and the flag state. Photocopies of the seaman's book and the discharge book do more for an application than a page of self-description.

Certificates that open doors

  • Certificate of Competency for the target rank, with STCW 2010 endorsements.
  • Advanced tanker and gas qualifications (CoP) if you are aiming at tankers or LNG.
  • MCU or equivalent medical fitness, ideally dated within the last twelve months.
  • A Marlins test result or documented English proficiency, which most European principals now require.

From rating to officer

ABLE Seaman and Oiler who plan to sit for the officer-of-the-watch exam should tell their crewing agency early. Some principals fund OOW training and exams for ratings who have already proven themselves on board, especially on tankers where the bridge team is small and continuity is valuable.

Questions to ask before signing

Before accepting any contract, confirm the wage in writing, the currency, the contract length, the joining port, and who pays for the flight and visa. A reputable manning agency under MLC 2006 will not charge you a recruitment fee, will give you a written contract in English, and will not ask you to sign anything you have not read. If a middleman asks for cash up front, walk away.

insights.title: STCW and medical document checklist for 2026
insights.lede: Avoid joining delays by keeping flag state endorsements, yellow fever certificates, seaman's book renewals, and MLC contract verification current.
insights.body:
Why documents fail at the gangway

The most common reason a seafarer misses a joining date is not a lack of experience. It is a certificate that lapsed three weeks before travel, a missing flag endorsement, or a medical certificate signed by a clinic the principal does not recognise. Almost every one of those is preventable with a checklist and a renewal diary.

The core set every officer should keep valid

  • Certificate of Competency (CoC) for the rank held, plus the STCW 2010 endorsements for the flag state of the vessel you are joining.
  • Seaman's book, with at least six blank pages and validity extending past the contract end date.
  • Passport, also valid past the contract end date and ideally past twelve months beyond it.
  • Medical fitness certificate from a clinic approved by the flag state or the principal, normally valid for twelve months or two years depending on the issuing authority.
  • Basic Safety Training (BST), refreshed within the past five years as required by STCW 2010.

Special certificates for special tonnage

Tanker officers need the appropriate Oil, Chemical, or Liquefied Gas familiarisation and advanced training certificates. Liquefied gas tonnage also expects a basic and advanced gas tanker certificate. Cruise and passenger vessel officers should confirm crowd management and crisis management requirements with the principal before joining.

Medical and travel documents

  • Yellow fever vaccination, if the itinerary includes countries on the WHO list.
  • Marlins test result, or another recognised English proficiency certificate.
  • A signed contract under MLC 2006, with wages, duration, and repatriation costs clearly stated.

Working with a manning agency

A legitimate agency under MLC 2006 does not charge seafarers a placement fee. We review every document against the principal's requirements before a candidate is proposed, tell you which certificates are about to lapse, and coordinate the visa, flag endorsement, and ticket. That is the standard Ardson Maritime holds itself to for every placement.

insights.title: How Indonesian seafarers can stand out to international principals
insights.lede: Maritime English, document hygiene, and sea-service records separate strong candidates from the rest of the pool.
insights.body:
English is the working language

Almost every international principal now uses the Marlins test, or an equivalent, as part of the screening process. A score of 75% or above on Marlins is the practical threshold for officers joining European-owned tonnage. Crew who prepare for Marlins properly pass it on the first attempt, and that single score often decides whether an application gets forwarded.

Document hygiene

Principals screen applications against a shortlist of documents. Having them current, legible, and easy to find removes friction from the process. We advise every candidate to keep a single PDF folder with:

  • Passport and seaman's book.
  • Certificate of Competency and STCW endorsements.
  • Medical fitness certificate.
  • Latest Marlins test result.
  • Sea service letters from each principal.
  • Up-to-date CV, with each contract on one row.

Reputation compounds

Sea service on a well-known principal, with a clean discharge and a good reference, is worth more than a higher salary offer elsewhere. Re-hire priority is the fastest route to a better rank and a longer contract. Officers who treat each contract as a long-term audition do better over a career than those who chase the highest short-term pay.
